title: Workflow agents: headless runs with a gated finish
summary: workflowAgent(spec) builds an agent for background jobs that never talk to a user. It finishes only after its check passes in the run, returns a validated structured output, and fails as budget_exhausted when it runs out of turns.
added: workflowAgent({ name, brief, tools, check, output, budget }) returns an ordinary Agent bundle with a WorkflowContract the loop enforces.
finish is the only exit: accepted only when the latest engine-recorded bash run of the check passed and no file was edited after it; a prose turn is a rejected finish.
output (JSON schema or zod) is validated inside the finish gate; the parsed value is AgentResult.output.
Conversational nudges (silent-tool, verbose-turn, prose checkpoint) are off by default; repeated-call, empty-turn, and capped-reply corrections stay on.
Agent bundles may suggest guardrails and budgets, merged per field under explicit engine options.
ask_questions, inbox chains, and delegation as a steerable team member are refused for workflows.
offers: Run setup or maintenance jobs that prove their result with a real command and hand back data instead of prose.
limits: The check-command match is honest-path enforcement, not a security boundary.
A check run inside a batch op does not count; run it with bash.
Only file edits through edit_file or batch withdraw a pass; a later mutating bash command does not.

title: Phases off means off everywhere
summary: A strategy with one phase, or with the phase intrinsic disabled, no longer leaks a phase into the prompt, events, hand-back, or thread record. A consumer's explicit resume phase is preserved.
added: Phase state is decided before thread resume and applied consistently: no set_phase, phase-discipline or current-phase prompt, phase_started/llm/tool phase fields, or AgentResult.phase when phases are off.
run_started.phases is empty when phases are off, and event phase fields are optional.
Fix: a consumer's explicit startPhase or resume phase is no longer overwritten by a stale phase from the thread record.
offers: Use a one-phase strategy without pretending that a phase the model cannot change is part of the run.
limits: Phase gating is unchanged for strategies with more than one enabled phase.
Phase ids remain approach labels, not permissions or proof of correctness.

title: A shared sandbox is detached, not paused, when a run ends
summary: Ending one run no longer parks a retained sandbox that other runs may still be using. Parking is an explicit provider.suspend call owned by the consumer.
added: Destroying a retained sandbox detaches the run instead of pausing E2B or stopping Docker, because several runs can share one retained workspace.
Optional provider.suspend: E2B pauses by id, Docker stops, Heyo scales to zero, and Local is a no-op.
E2B lifecycle.onTimeout: pause remains the idle safety net for a retained sandbox.
E2B adoption retries connect and workspace checks; WorkspaceUnavailableError is treated as transient, while only SandboxNotFoundError is gone.
offers: Share one durable worker environment across runs without one finished run taking the machine away from the others.
limits: Anchor does not choose an idle or parking policy; call provider.suspend when the consumer decides the sandbox should sleep.
Live provider behavior remains credential-gated and provider-specific.

title: A transient adopt failure no longer splits a thread
summary: A lock or control-plane hiccup while adopting a sandbox is retried instead of being mistaken for a dead sandbox and replaced with a fresh one.
added: openSandboxSession retries transient adoption failures with backoff; it clears the stored pointer and builds fresh only when the provider says the sandbox is truly gone.
SandboxGoneError, isSandboxGone, and optional provider.isGone distinguish a missing sandbox from a transient error.
E2B classifies not-found as gone while transitioning, lock, and timeout failures stay transient.
E2B configureGit is idempotent and retries a config lock, including a stale lock left by a killed git process.
Local, Docker, and Heyo report gone/transient outcomes consistently.
offers: Keep a thread on one sandbox when two openers race, instead of silently splitting its work across two environments.
limits: Retries are bounded; a persistent non-gone failure fails loudly rather than inventing a replacement sandbox.
A provider that cannot classify absence cannot recover a truly lost sandbox automatically.

title: The split ledger tools are the only face of the contract
summary: The deprecated update_ledger shim is removed after the seven focused ledger tools proved safer for models to use.
added: The contract now exposes add_requirement, set_requirement_status, link_evidence, verify_requirement, set_next_step, add_failure, and clear_failure.
The old update_ledger op-field surface and its inference path are gone.
Tests and prompts use the focused tool names only.
offers: A missing field becomes a schema error on a single-purpose tool instead of a mixed-op ledger call that stalls a turn.
limits: This is a tool-surface change: consumers or prompts that still name update_ledger must use the split tools.
The ledger data shape itself is unchanged.

title: Supervision for long delegations
summary: Workers get bounded budgets, a wrap-up and partial hand-back, steer and nudge channels, a cancel grace, and a stalled-worker signal. This release includes the unpublished 0.8.4 budget work.
added: Per-child BudgetTracker with steps, wall-clock, and USD limits; explicit delegate budget wins, then member defaults, then a capped derived default.
At 80% of budget the child gets one wrap-up directive; at 100% it hands back a partial result with reason budget_exhausted and the leader continues.
steer_worker and onProgress steer/nudge handles share one bounded, length-capped channel.
Cancel waits at most cancelGraceMs (default 5s) for the call in flight.
A child's wall-clock deadline is enforced at every tool boundary through an AbortSignal.
A child with no event for stallAfterMs (default 10 minutes) emits one progress record with stalled: true; activity resets the window.
offers: Run a crew with proportionate budgets and a supervisor that can redirect or wrap up a worker before it burns the whole run.
limits: The engine signals a stall; it does not cancel or nudge a worker by itself.
A tool that ignores its AbortSignal can still run to its own end.
0.8.4 was prepared but not published; its features ship here.

title: One tool per ledger operation
summary: The contract tools are split so each action has a tight schema, and contract bookkeeping is no longer captured as evidence about the work.
added: Seven focused tools replace the single mixed-op update_ledger surface: add_requirement, set_requirement_status, link_evidence, verify_requirement, set_next_step, add_failure, clear_failure.
Every focused tool uses additionalProperties: false and omits the op field.
The deprecated update_ledger shim infers an op only where the fields name exactly one.
Contract tools are excluded from ledger evidence capture.
offers: A model that sends the wrong field gets a schema-shaped correction instead of silently mixing an add with a status or failure.
limits: The shim remains temporarily for compatibility and is removed in 0.8.6.
Tool names are a prompt-cache and consumer-integration surface.

title: Product-neutral package examples
summary: Repository short-name resolution stays in the package, with product-specific examples removed from its source and tests.
added: The repo short-name resolver still accepts a unique short name for an attached repository.
Product-specific fixture names were replaced with neutral examples.
No package behavior changed.
offers: Keep the SDK product-neutral while preserving convenient repository addressing.
limits: Two repositories that share a short name remain ambiguous and require the full name.

title: Extend a settled contract
summary: A finished ledger can be offered for follow-up work, and update_ledger can infer the operation when a payload names exactly one.
added: EngineOptions.extendLedger keeps a settled injected ledger attached so follow-up requirements can extend the same contract.
update_ledger infers set_status, link_evidence, add_failure, or add_requirement when the provided fields point to exactly one operation.
A repository short name resolves when only one attached repository has it.
offers: Continue a completed task under its original evidence trail instead of starting from an empty contract.
limits: An ambiguous payload is refused rather than guessed.
A short repository name shared by two repos remains unresolved.

title: Retained sandboxes survive long runs
summary: E2B renews a retained sandbox lifetime while it is in use and pauses instead of killing it on timeout. Delegations also fan out after a turn that opens with ordinary calls.
added: E2B retained sandboxes use lifecycle.onTimeout: pause, so disk and memory survive an idle timeout.
A keepalive renews the E2B lifetime while the sandbox is in use, at most every ten minutes.
Throwaway E2B sandboxes keep the provider kill behavior.
Fix: a leader turn that starts with ordinary calls such as set_phase still fans out its delegations.
0.7.2 was prepared but not published; its dispatch fix is included here.
offers: Run a task longer than the sandbox lifetime without losing the workspace underneath it.
limits: Keepalive renewal is best-effort; the idle timeout remains the provider's safety net.
This release does not change disposable-sandbox cleanup.

title: Ledger errors tell the model what to send
summary: The update_ledger schema explains which operation each field belongs to, and failed calls show the shape to retry.
added: Field descriptions name their operation: text for add_requirement, requirementId for status/link/verify, claim and evidenceId for evidence.
Missing add_requirement text and add_failure failure errors include an example payload.
The description lists every operation and its required fields.
offers: Recover from a malformed ledger call in one turn instead of repeating it verbatim.
limits: This is guidance and validation, not a new ledger capability.
The mixed-op tool is replaced by focused tools in 0.8.3.

title: Admission and worker trees: the consumer decides what runs, and where
summary: A consumer can check every delegation before it runs and refuse it with a reason, so plans, approvals and gates are enforced in code rather than trusted to the leader's prompt.
added: team.admit({ worker, member, role, readOnly, task, item, base }) runs before any workspace or child run; { ok: false, reason } is returned to the leader verbatim.
delegate accepts item — the consumer's work-item id — when admission is installed; it reaches the workspace hook and the result's meta.item.
team.workspace may return a sandbox: scopedSandbox(sandbox, dir) is a view whose commands and file tools default to the worker's tree, so a worker's edits land in its own worktree.
Fix: delegated runs no longer take a git snapshot at their conclusion; checkpoints are the leader's.
closeLspSessions(sandbox) (anchor-ai-sdk/lsp) stops every language server started for a sandbox or view; servers otherwise keep running for the life of the sandbox.
warmLspSessions(sandbox, { servers, repos, files }) starts the language servers an agent will use and loads their projects ahead of its first call, sharing the tools' sessions.
offers: Put a human-approval gate or a dependency check in front of a crew, with the engine guaranteeing no worker starts until it passes.
limits: Anchor knows nothing about plans or approvals; the consumer stores and decides them.
item is free text; the consumer validates it.

title: Crews: workers with memory, working in parallel
summary: A team is now a crew: the leader names worker instances, sends follow-ups to the worker that did the work, runs different workers in parallel, and the consumer decides where each one works.
added: delegate({ agent, worker }): workers are instances of a roster member, so a leader can run frontend-1 and frontend-2. Events carry worker and role.
team.sessions: a worker's conversation is an ordinary engine thread, so a later delegate to the same worker resumes it; fresh: true starts over.
Parallel delegation: different workers in one leader turn run concurrently through resource-grouped dispatch, bounded by team.maxParallel (default 4).
team.workspace: the consumer returns the repos a worker sees and a sentence about where it works (e.g. a git worktree per writer); base lets a worker continue another's branch.
Live frames and projectConversation keep each delegation's stream separate and nest it on the leader's delegate part.
ToolContext.team tells a tool which worker (and member, role) is calling it.
Fix: a coding agent can be a read-only member or evaluator: tools removed by the read-only filter no longer fail the strategy's requiredTools check.
offers: Build a captain-and-crew: read-only researchers and reviewers in parallel, writers on their own branches, and fixes routed back to whoever wrote the code.
limits: Depth is one; workers cannot delegate.
Anchor never creates worktrees or merges branches; that is the workspace hook's job.
A worker name belongs to one member within a leader run; persisted sessions do not record the member.
No automatic review loop; the leader decides.

title: Delegated teams and dependency-aware contracts
summary: Anchor can delegate one level to named workers and evaluators, coordinate through leased task and mailbox contracts, and order contract requirements as a real dependency graph.
added: One-level delegated subagents: EngineOptions.team, the delegate tool, leader/worker/evaluator roles, result-only returns, per-member budgets, and agent-tagged trace events.
Consumer-owned team coordination contracts: TeamTaskStore with lease-based claim/release and AgentMailbox with addressed claim/ack/release, plus in-memory adapters.

Contract requirement dependency graph: custom ids, dependsOn edges, forward references, cycle/unknown/self/duplicate/superseded-edge validation, derived readiness, topological rendering, and finish-gate enforcement.
CodingPromptOptions.phasesIntro lets consumers replace the phase-list intro without forking the coding prompt.
create_task accepts up to 30 atomic requirement items instead of 12, and the eval harness now uses the RunInput message shape.
offers: Compose a leader with named helpers, give each a bounded role and budget, and make multi-step contracts explicit without turning phases into a dependency chain.
limits: Teams are one level, serial, same-sandbox, and result-only. There is no parallel worker execution, workspace isolation/merge, scheduler, or team UI.
TeamTaskStore and AgentMailbox are contracts with in-memory adapters only; durable Postgres and product UI remain consumer-owned.
Requirement dependencies are orthogonal to phases and remain optional. There is no migration, no automatic edge creation, and no team/task-board DAG.
Delegated child-session continuation and automatic worker-to-evaluator feedback loops are not implemented.
No new benchmark result is claimed for v0.5.0. Sailor/Sailor-cloud adoption is a separate change.

title: Serializable tool results and trace payloads
summary: Tool-result metadata, ledger evidence, and trace redaction now cross persistence boundaries as detached plain JSON.
added: ToolResult.meta is typed as plain JsonObject; the dispatcher copies every result into a detached JSON value before emitting, evidence capture, or journaling.
toPlainJson and toPlainJsonObject normalize cycles, BigInts, functions, Dates, Maps, Sets, Errors, and class instances at the boundary.
The create_task ledger cycle is fixed by returning identifiers instead of the live ledger in tool-result metadata.
Trace redaction now runs over the same serializable copy, so one bad payload cannot stall a sink.
offers: Tool results, evidence, and trace events are safe to persist in databases and files without hidden aliases or circular structures.
limits: Breaking: ToolResult.meta is now JsonObject. Consumer tools returning interface-typed or non-JSON meta fail to compile; use toPlainJsonObject at the boundary.
0.3.1 was an under-versioned publication of this breaking change; use 0.4.0.
No new benchmark result is claimed for v0.4.0.

title: Peer repositories and progressive skills
summary: Anchor can operate one tool call at a time across peer repositories, parallelize mutations by repository, root LSP per repo, and load consumer-owned skills on demand.
added: Peer-repository workspaces: RepoRef, EngineOptions.repos, repo-aware bash and run_tests, repo-attributed edit_file paths, and per-repo LSP roots.
Resource-keyed mutation dispatch: different repositories may run concurrently; same-repository calls serialize; no-repository and effectful calls stay in the global ordered group.
run_tests now reports the repository and a tree hash computed in that repository, enabling attributable per-repo evidence.
Skills: consumer-owned SkillProvider, deterministic renderSkillIndex, and a bounded read-only load_skill tool with resource paths and trace metadata.
offers: Build agents that work across real peer-repo workspaces without collapsing results into one blob, and give them a compact skill index with on-demand bodies.
limits: Checkpoints remain single-root; per-repo snapshots are consumer-owned through EngineOptions.snapshot.
Skills are instructions only. Storage, discovery, precedence, trust, UI, and sandbox materialization remain consumer-owned.
No new benchmark result is claimed for v0.3.0.
Sailor/Sailor-cloud adoption is a separate change.

title: Contracts created by the agent
summary: One agent, message-shaped input, agent-created task contracts, claimed evidence, and the existing prose verifier behind a judge seam.
added: RunInput replaces RunTask; runAgent takes a message delta, and renderInboxTurn preserves one message per inbox row.
The create_task intrinsic lets the agent create a phase-owned contract mid-run; the engine derives the request source from user messages.
Evidence links require a claim, and op: verify links and verifies in one call. Phase transitions judge the outgoing phase and name unmet requirements.
The existing prose verifier is available through the Judge seam as llmJudge; verdicts are per requirement.
finish({ success: false }) ends honestly with ok: false and open failures.
offers: One agent and one tool surface for every turn, with contracts created only when the work calls for one and a verifier that explains what is still unproven.
limits: This is a breaking release: intent routing, RunTask.task, and compile-at-start defaults are removed.
A forced phase transition after the rejection limit leaves the requirement in progress; finish remains blocked.
The verifier is a guard against unsupported completion, not proof of correctness.
No new benchmark result is claimed for v0.2.0.

title: Task state, images, and preview endpoints
summary: Turn routing respects an active task contract, task compaction preserves a durable handoff, image references reach vision models, and E2B can expose a guest port.
added: Ledger-aware turn routing: an active required ledger keeps auto follow-ups on the task path; explicit intent still wins; inbox batches re-route per claimed run.
Structured task compaction: an SDK-owned CompactionHandoff is persisted on the thread and replaces the old summarized span with pinned ledger/task state plus a recent verbatim tail.

Image context: ImageAttachment references on RunTask, user messages, and inbox messages, with OpenAI-compatible image_url serialization. Consumers own bytes, storage, validation, signed URLs, and retention.
E2B preview ports: Sandbox.exposePort(port) and an explicit previewPort capability. E2B returns a public HTTPS URL; other providers declare false.
Consumer implementation docs: Postgres ThreadStore, InboxStore, OperationStore, and SandboxStore examples, plus the compaction handoff.
Site release timeline, per-tag GitHub release notes, and the complete v0.1.7 benchmark page.
offers: Keep task contracts alive across follow-ups, reset long task context without losing requirements, pass images through one reference contract, and hand a preview URL to the product while keeping preview UI and policy consumer-owned.
limits: Image support currently targets OpenAI-compatible image_url parts. Native Anthropic/Gemini image blocks are still deferred; PDFs, audio, and video are consumer preprocessing concerns.
E2B preview URLs are public by default. Anchor does not add authentication, health checks, iframes, logs, or idle-stop policy.
Abortable one-shot exec from PR #9 was not merged; openProcess cancellation exists, but synchronous exec still waits for its deadline.
No v0.1.9 benchmark result is recorded. The complete benchmark record remains v0.1.7 at 2fbc92b.

title: Evidence-backed tasks and extensible machines
summary: An opt-in verification layer tracks what remains, while new sandbox and tool interfaces make it easier to build your own agent environment.
added: Opt-in verifier mode: an append-only progress ledger, requirement compiler, automatic evidence references, intent routing, and phase/finish checks. Ledger state persists through the existing thread store; compiler and verifier usage counts against the run budget.
First-class structured output through responseFormat and completeStructured, plus a terminal-native agent bundle.
Durable operation recovery for external-effect tools: stable operation IDs, acknowledgment, reconciliation, and a consumer-supplied operation store.
Optional Sandbox.openProcess with stdin/stdout streams, wait, kill, timeout, abort, and destroy cleanup across Local, Docker, E2B, and Heyo. Docker also gains background-job poll/kill support.
A common ImagePublisher contract and anchor image publish CLI for Docker images, E2B templates, and Heyo artifacts. Heyo accepts per-sandbox artifact refs.

Optional anchor-ai-sdk/lsp entry point: TypeScript/JavaScript diagnostics, definition, references, and document symbols over process streams. Language servers are installed by the consumer in the sandbox image.
A public tool-result boundary caps consumer tool output. Benchmark workflows support pinned refs and record version/SHA metadata, with SWE-bench Lite/Pro and Terminal-Bench external comparisons.
offers: Build agents that track requirements and supporting evidence, recover uncertain external operations, and reuse provider-native environments without putting LSP or registry logic in the core loop.
limits: Verifier checks are opt-in, not a correctness certificate. The default verifier outage policy allows with a warning; use onError: block for stricter behavior.
Heyo process streams use a PTY: stderr is merged into stdout, EOF uses Ctrl-D semantics, and the transport exposes no drain signal. Raw byte-sensitive LSP operation on Heyo is not live-verified.

Image publishing was tested with injected runners/fake CLIs, not live registries. Docker requires its daemon/login, E2B requires its optional SDK/API key, and Heyo requires an installed, authenticated heyctl. Daytona remains a stub.
Abortable one-shot exec from PR #9 was not merged. ProcessOptions.signal applies to openProcess, not cancellation of existing exec calls.
The interrupted v0.1.8 benchmark is not a completed evaluation of this release. No performance improvement is claimed here.

title: Background work joins the conversation
summary: Long-running commands can deliver their results into a continuing thread instead of leaving the agent waiting without feedback.
added: Background-result delivery at turn boundaries and before model calls, with completion messages persisted into the conversation.
InboxStore and run-chain primitives for queued messages, interjections, and carrying background jobs across turns.
Docker egress: none disconnects networks after setup, so installation and clone can finish before the agent phase loses network access.
Verbosity accounting measures visible output rather than treating reasoning tokens as user-visible prose; dispatch and guardrail mechanics were separated internally.
Build-first examples, reviewed README claims, and refreshed documentation website.
offers: Keep a thread responsive while commands finish, and let the host decide how to store inbox state and restrict Docker network access.
limits: The archived v0.1.7-2fbc92b benchmark measured later source than the v0.1.7 tag (08472b1). It must not be presented as a measurement of this exact tag.
Durable external-operation recovery and the verification ledger arrived after this tag, in v0.1.8.

title: E2B and bounded generation
summary: A second remote sandbox adapter and tighter generation controls broaden where agents run and help recover from unproductive turns.
added: E2B sandbox adapter with template-based boot, lifecycle/adoption, checkpoints, and offline tests. localPath is rejected explicitly on the remote backend.
Per-call output caps and assistant-text elision, continuation after a capped reply, and bounded course correction for empty turns and repeated calls.
E2B credential mint reuse and explicit retained-sandbox adoption behavior.
Eval runner imports the current repository build and can pin provider settings; E2B task verification and environment examples were added.
offers: Choose E2B without replacing the agent loop, and bound an individual runaway generation instead of only the total run.
limits: E2B boots prepared templates, not arbitrary Docker images at sandbox creation. Remote live tests are opt-in.

title: Phase discipline belongs to the runtime
summary: The engine keeps phase guidance consistent with the tools it actually exposes.
added: An intrinsic phase-discipline prompt block, gated by the same phase flag that registers the phase tool.
Clearer phase-transition guidance without turning approach labels into permission gates.
Sandbox image-source and boot-cost guidance, plus eval-baseline cleanup.
offers: Custom strategies get consistent phase bookkeeping without copying the default coding prompt.
limits: Phases describe the approach; they do not prove that work is correct or authorize publishing.

title: Use the right tool for the read
summary: The shell tool points agents toward the dedicated search and file-reading interfaces.
added: bash guidance directs repository searches to search and file inspection to read_file rather than unbounded grep/cat output.
Decision records describe the read-only tool boundary and deferred agent-team design.
offers: More predictable, paged observations through the existing small toolbox.
limits: Agent teams are a design note, not a shipped capability in this release.

title: Detach long commands, keep their deadline
summary: Heyo commands can return control while a guest-side job continues under its own lifetime contract.
added: backgroundAfterSecs, background job handles, pollJob, and killJob for Heyo execution.
background_started events carry the job lifetime so the consumer can retain and manage the sandbox.
Trace rendering no longer treats zero reasoning tokens as a reasoning block.
offers: Hand slow commands back to the host without replaying their launch or losing the guest deadline.
limits: Automatic engine delivery of background results came later, in v0.1.7. This is not an interactive stdin stream.

title: Concurrent reads and recoverable guest jobs
summary: A job registry prevents one missing completion receipt from blocking the sandbox indefinitely.
added: Heyo guest-job tracking, with lost receipts failing the affected command rather than wedging later work.
Read-only execution can run concurrently while mutation ordering remains protected.
Eval assets organized into per-benchmark folders.
offers: Recover from uncertain tool transport and overlap independent reads without parallelizing coupled writes.
limits: Background detachment/polling was added in v0.1.3, after this tag.

title: Make real phase transitions visible
summary: The coding prompt asks the agent to label changes in approach when they happen.
added: Prompt guidance to call set_phase at real transitions instead of leaving the phase trail stale.
Runnable quickstart and non-coding examples, README accuracy work, CI fixes, and the first standalone website.
offers: A clearer approach trail for consumers following a run, with examples for more than coding tasks.
limits: The intrinsic runtime phase block arrived later, in v0.1.5.

title: The standalone agent harness SDK
summary: Anchor's initial tagged release brings the shared loop, tools, machine contract, and run state into a reusable TypeScript package.
added: Streaming OpenAI-compatible model client, chat/coding bundles, custom strategies and tools, and step/token/known-cost budgets.
Shell, file read/edit, search, test, and finish primitives; guardrails, compaction, durable notes, thread persistence, and pause/resume.
SandboxProvider seam with Local, Docker, and Heyo adapters, git checkpoints, retention/adoption, credential callbacks, and conformance tooling.
Budget revival planning, structured execution evidence, sequenced/redacted trace sinks, and repository-owned evals.
offers: Compose an agent around your model and tools while keeping storage, credentials, provider choice, and product policy in the host.
limits: Early alpha: pin exact versions and test integrations. Local executes with host permissions and is not an isolation boundary.
